To: Operations Leadership Team
From: Service Operations Manager
Subject: Staffing Mix Review and Cost-Optimized Assignment for the Service Center

Purpose
We are conducting a comprehensive review of how we assign staff across our multi-station service center. The aim is to match skills to demand in a way that protects service quality and minimizes total hourly staffing cost.

Current Situation
Our service center consists of multiple help desks, counters, and department-specific stations. Each station experiences a different, known pace of customer arrivals measured in customers per hour. We have multiple types of staff with distinct skill sets. Their productivity varies by station: some handle customers faster in certain environments, and some cannot be assigned to specific stations due to qualifications. Handling speed is tracked as average minutes per customer at each station for each staff type.

Staffing Challenge
The assignment problem is complex because:
- Demand and capability vary by station, and staff performance is not uniform across stations.
- Some staff-station pairings are not permitted due to qualifications.
- Each staff type has a limited pool of available headcount.
- Hourly labor costs differ by staff type, so the fastest option is not always the most cost-effective.
We need to navigate these trade-offs across a large set of potential assignments to find the most efficient mix.

Service Quality Policies and Operating Requirements
- Demand-capacity alignment with buffer: Demand is measured hourly, while service capability is described in minutes per customer. When planning coverage, we must reconcile these measures so that the combined capacity of the assigned team at each station comfortably exceeds expected arrivals. This buffer ensures stability and prevents the operation from running too hot.
- Target occupancy: We maintain a cap on how busy staff should be on average at a station. Assignments must keep expected load within this policy to safeguard wait times and prevent burnout.
- Minimum coverage: Each station requires a baseline number of staff on post for consistent customer coverage, contingency handling, and handoffs.
- Qualifications: Staff may only be assigned where they are certified to work; restricted pairings are not allowed.
- Availability limits: We cannot exceed the number of people available in each staff type.
- Cost discipline: Because hourly rates differ, we must find the least-cost combination that satisfies all of the above.

Planning Approach
We will construct a station-by-station placement that:
- Establishes minimum coverage at every station first.
- Filters out non-qualified assignments before considering options.
- Adds capacity where expected arrival volume requires it, keeping team throughput comfortably ahead of demand under the occupancy policy.
- Chooses among feasible staff types based on effectiveness at the station and hourly cost, favoring the lowest-cost combination that meets service policies.
- Respects the available headcount for each staff type to avoid over-allocation.

Deliverables and Outcome
The result will be a recommended assignment for each station indicating the number and type of personnel, along with an estimate of expected load relative to the policy cap. The plan will:
- Meet or exceed demand at every station with a safety margin.
- Keep expected occupancy within policy limits.
- Satisfy minimum coverage requirements at all stations.
- Use only qualified staff.
- Stay within available headcount for each staff type.
- Minimize total hourly staffing cost.

Next Steps
Upon confirmation of the policy thresholds and input data, we will produce the recommended assignment and conduct sensitivity checks for changes in arrivals or staffing availability. We will also highlight any stations where coverage is tight so that cross-training, hiring, or policy adjustments can be considered.
